title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. College Saturday (Oct. 17) and NFL Sunday (Oct. 18), graded. Then Monday night and next weekend.

paragraphs: Every pick below is graded against the line printed on its card when the game kicked off, not the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss.
What got graded: 52 college games from Saturday and 12 NFL games from Sunday. College cards carried a side from the Cover Writer and from each handicapper, plus a Cover Writer total.

What did not get graded, because no pick was published: Thursday's NFL game (Seattle 14 at Denver 17, overtime), Thursday's college games (East Carolina 17 at UAB 30, Georgia Southern 23 at Old Dominion 15, Colorado State 27 at Texas State 66) and Friday's college games (Memphis 17 at Tulane 31, Washington 38 at Purdue 26, Appalachian State 35 at Coastal Carolina 32). Three FCS-opponent games (The Citadel at Texas A&M, Charleston Southern at Clemson, Elon at Stanford) had no pick from The Formula, so it is not graded there.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on Mississippi State +17.5 (card line: LSU −17.5). Mississippi State lost by 31. Missed by 13.5. The Cover Writer projected LSU 34, Mississippi State 18.

The Cover Writer expected LSU's missing linebackers and Mississippi State's extra week of rest to keep this from getting out of hand. With redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett at quarterback in place of Kamario Taylor, Mississippi State did not score. Sam Leavitt's third touchdown pass, 17 yards to Jackson Harris with 6:12 left in the first half, made it 21-0, and the margin never came back inside 17.5. Mississippi State turned it over on downs at the LSU 28 and the LSU 30 in the fourth quarter.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Texas −11.5 (card line). Texas lost by 3. Missed by 14.5. The Cover Writer projected Texas 34, Florida 14.

The Cover Writer's case was Texas's defense against a Florida team starting a first-time quarterback, Tramell Jones Jr. Jones threw two touchdown passes to Lacota Dippre, and Florida led 20-17 in the fourth quarter. The moment that ended it came with 8:34 left: Arch Manning was stopped for a 3-yard loss on fourth down at the Texas 45. Florida scored from there, Jadan Baugh's 11-yard run for 27-17.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 48). The final total was 51. Missed by 0.5.
The Under was alive until 4:21 was left. Cam Coleman's 9-yard touchdown catch from Manning made it 51 points, half a point over.
Missed: Letdown Watch on Texas A&M −46.5 (card line). Texas A&M won by 41. Missed by 5.5.

Texas A&M led 34-0 after three quarters and needed to win by 47. Aaron Gregory's 12-yard touchdown catch from Brady Hart with 5:47 left made it 41-0, and that was the last score. The Citadel missed a 47-yard field goal with 1:13 left.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Georgia −19.5 (card line). Georgia lost by 3. Missed by 22.5.

Auburn led 24-14 after three quarters and won outright. Georgia's last real chance ended when Gunner Stockton fumbled near midfield with 58 seconds left; C. Sigler forced it and S. Smith-Reed recovered for Auburn.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 47). The final total was 51. Missed by 1.5.

The Under held until the last play. It was 24-24, a 48-point game, when Georgia was flagged for roughing the passer on G. Harris Jr. with 15 seconds left, 15 yards to the Georgia 19. Alex McPherson's 34-yard field goal on the final play made it 51.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Missouri +5.5 (card line: Ole Miss −5.5). Missouri lost by 28. Missed by 22.5. The Cover Writer projected Ole Miss 31, Missouri 26.

The Cover Writer expected Missouri's defense and its running game to keep it close all the way. Trinidad Chambliss threw touchdown passes of 10, 21 and 17 yards in the first half, and Missouri never scored again after its opening field goal. Its last drive ended with L. Barnes' interception at the Ole Miss 1.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Letdown Watch on Alabama −7.5 (card line). Alabama lost by 16. Missed by 23.5. The Cover Writer projected Alabama 28, Tennessee 20.

The Cover Writer's case was Alabama's offense and defense against a Tennessee quarterback, George MacIntyre, making his second career start. Tennessee won by 16. Cooper Ranvier kicked four first-half field goals, and DeSean Bishop scored on two 5-yard runs. Alabama's last drive ended with an interception by K. Lee in the end zone.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Vanderbilt −6 (card line). Vanderbilt lost by 10. Missed by 16.
Arkansas led 28-21 after Cam Settles' 3-yard run with 9 seconds left in the third. Vanderbilt's best drive of the fourth went 63 yards in 14 plays and ended with an interception by M. Mitchell.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 50). The final total was 52. Missed by 1.5.
The total was 49 with 24 seconds left. Max Gilbert's 39-yard field goal made it 52.
Missed: Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Oklahoma −6.5 (card line). Oklahoma lost by 8. Missed by 14.5.

Kentucky won outright. Willie Rodriguez's 12-yard touchdown catch from Kenny Minchey put Kentucky ahead 14-13 with 12:53 left, and Jordan Castell returned an interception 41 yards for a touchdown with 1:17 left.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Cincinnati +1.5 (card line: West Virginia −1.5). Cincinnati lost by 3. Missed by 1.5. The Cover Writer projected Cincinnati 34, West Virginia 33.

Everyone on the card was on Cincinnati, and the Cover Writer's own line was "One late stop should settle it." Nobody stopped anybody. The game was tied six times, each time after Cincinnati scored and West Virginia answered. Cam Cook's 40-yard touchdown catch from Michael Hawkins Jr. tied it 42-42 with 3:44 left. At 42-42, Cincinnati +1.5 was covering. Jack Cassidy's 35-yard field goal as time expired ended that.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Kansas +3.5 (card line: Kansas State −3.5). Kansas lost by 11. Missed by 7.5.

Kansas led 24-18 in the third. Two fourth-quarter plays hurt it most. Isaiah Marshall was intercepted at the goal line by L. Bartley with 10:02 left, and Kansas State scored on its next possession, Jaron Tibbs' 9-yard catch from Avery Johnson for 32-24, a drive helped by a Kansas face-mask penalty. Then Marshall broke a 46-yard touchdown run, and another Kansas face-mask penalty took it off the board. That touchdown would have made it 32-30 before the extra point.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Arizona State +15.5 (card line: Texas Tech −15.5). Arizona State lost by 28. Missed by 12.5.
Texas Tech led 43-10 at the half. It started with Ben Roberts' 24-yard interception return, and J'Koby Williams added touchdown runs of 62 and 38 yards.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 47). The final total was 78. Missed by 28.5.

The Under rested on Texas Tech's defense. The defense scored, and the offense scored 46 more. The total passed 49.5 before halftime, on Coy Eakin's 11-yard catch from Will Hammond with 31 seconds left in the second quarter. The final total was 78.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Baylor −5.5 (card line). Baylor lost by 11. Missed by 16.5. The Cover Writer projected Baylor 27, TCU 20.
The Cover Writer's case was home field and TCU missing two offensive linemen. Baylor scored two field goals all night. Its last two drives both ended on fourth-down incompletions.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Follow The Money on Notre Dame −10.5 (card line). Notre Dame lost by 4. Missed by 14.5. The Cover Writer projected Notre Dame 28, BYU 17.
BYU won outright. Notre Dame led 24-21 after Jonaz Walton's 3-yard run and two-point run with 9:31 left. Bear Bachmeier's 6-yard touchdown pass to Walker Lyons with 1:47 left won it.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 47.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 52. Missed by 4.5.
Lyons' touchdown also took the total from 45 to 52.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Houston −4.5 (card line). Houston won by 3. Missed by 1.5. The Cover Writer projected Houston 36, Oklahoma State 29.
Houston led 35-25 after Koby Young's 48-yard catch with 9:48 left. Drew Mestemaker's 8-yard touchdown pass to Justin Bowick with 4:54 left cut it to 3, and nobody scored after that.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Utah −14.5 (card line). Utah won by 3. Missed by 11.5. The Cover Writer projected Utah 32, Colorado 17.

The Cover Writer's pick went against all five handicappers, who all had Colorado. Colorado scored 17 straight points in the third quarter to lead 17-13. Utah took the lead back but never led by 15: Braden Pegan's 6-yard catch from Devon Dampier with 3:43 left made it 27-17, and Colorado answered.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 49). The final total was 51. Missed by 1.5.
The Under stood at 44 points with 1:21 left. DeAndre Moore Jr.'s 2-yard touchdown catch from Isaac Wilson made it 51.
Missed: Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Clemson −43.5 (card line). Clemson won by 37. Missed by 6.5.
Clemson led 34-0 at the half and scored 3 more points. Nolan Hauser's 44-yard field goal early in the fourth was the last score. Clemson's last drive ended on downs at the Charleston Southern 27.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Pittsburgh −6.5 (card line). Pittsburgh lost by 6. Missed by 12.5. The Cover Writer projected Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15.

The Cover Writer's case was Pitt's defense making up for a true freshman quarterback's first start. Pitt led 12-0 early, then Boston College scored 21 straight. The last of those, Mason McKenzie's 69-yard touchdown pass to Landon Wright 46 seconds into the second half, made it 21-12. Pitt never got closer than 3.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 42.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 39). The final total was 48. Missed by 5.5.
The Under was gone with 13:02 left, when Evan Dickens' 1-yard run made it 45 points. The final total was 48.
Missed: The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Georgia Tech +8.5 (card line: Virginia Tech −8.5). Georgia Tech lost by 10. Missed by 1.5.

Georgia Tech trailed 34-17 and got within 10, which was not enough. The key play: Aidan Birr missed a 32-yard field goal with 10:26 left. Jaiven Plummer's 6-yard touchdown catch with 5:20 left then made it 34-24. Had Birr's kick been good, that touchdown would have left a 7-point game.
Missed: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Duke −3 (card line). Duke lost by 4. Missed by 7.

Duke rallied from 17-0 and led 20-17 after Nate Sheppard's 7-yard catch from Walker Eget with 4:39 left. Jaylen McGill's 24-yard touchdown run with 1:53 left put North Carolina back in front, and K. Dopson III intercepted Eget at the North Carolina 15 with 19 seconds left.
Missed: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Miami −20.5 (card line). Miami won by 8. Missed by 12.5. The Cover Writer projected Miami 41, Florida State 19.

Florida State led 21-14 after three quarters and did not go away. Duce Robinson's 75-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Daniels tied it 28-28 with 2:39 left. Miami won in the second overtime on Malachi Toney's 3-yard touchdown catch, and Toney threw the two-point pass himself.
Missed: Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Stanford −34.5 (card line). Stanford won by 27. Missed by 7.5.

Stanford led 34-0 after Micah Ford's 81-yard run early in the fourth, and the extra point failed. That left Stanford exactly 34 points ahead, half a point short. Elon's Kamerin McDowell-Moore then scored on an 18-yard run, and Stanford's last scoring chance ended with a fumble at the Elon 1 that went through the end zone for a touchback.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Louisville −14.5 (card line). Louisville won by 8. Missed by 6.5.

Syracuse, playing its third quarterback option, led 23-21 in the second quarter and trailed only 28-26 with 12:45 left. Keyjuan Brown's 5-yard run with 7:34 left made it 34-26, and the extra point failed. Syracuse's last two drives ended on downs, but an 8-point loss covers 14.5.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on California +10 (card line: Wake Forest −10). California lost by 34. Missed by 24.
Wake Forest led 41-0 after three quarters. Dominick Barry caught three of Gio Lopez's touchdown passes.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 53.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 54). The final total was 48. Missed by 5.5.
Wake Forest did its part with 41. California scored 7, on Mason Mini's 28-yard catch in the fourth, and its last drive ended on downs. The total was 48.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Indiana +3 (card line: Ohio State −3). Indiana lost by 4. Missed by 1. The Cover Writer projected Ohio State 26, Indiana 25.

Indiana needed to lose by 2 or fewer. Ohio State's two-point try failed after Jeremiah Smith's 38-yard touchdown catch, leaving it 19-7. Josh Hoover's 19-yard touchdown pass to Nick Marsh and a two-point pass to Turbo Richard made it 19-15 with 10:30 left. Indiana's last drive ended with a fourth-down incompletion for Marsh with 1:07 left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 51). The final total was 34. Missed by 16.5.
The Cover Writer expected the offenses to win out. Two top-15 defenses held it to 34 points.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Northwestern −7 (card line). Northwestern won by 3. Missed by 4. The Cover Writer projected Northwestern 30, Michigan State 20.

Northwestern won on the last kick but never covered at any point. It trailed 21-13 in the fourth, tied it on Aidan Chiles' 1-yard run and two-point pass, blocked Michigan State's 33-yard field goal try with a minute left, and won on Jackson Kleather's 34-yarder with 2 seconds left. A 3-point win, 4 points short.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 50). The final total was 45. Missed by 4.5.
The game had two blocked field goals, a Kleather try in the second quarter and Michigan State's late one. The total was 45.
Missed: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Maryland −6 (card line). Maryland lost by 7. Missed by 13.

Tied 23-23 late in the third, Rutgers then scored two touchdowns: Clay Thevenin's 7-yard run and Antwan Raymond's 2-yard run for 37-23. Maryland's last drive ended on a fourth-down incompletion with 19 seconds left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 55.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 53). The final total was 67. Missed by 11.5.
The total passed 55.5 on Raymond's touchdown with 4:03 left. The final total was 67. The card's forecast of gusts around 37 mph did not slow either offense.
Missed: Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Michigan −6.5 (card line). Michigan won by 3. Missed by 3.5.

Michigan led 21-11 after Tommy Carr's 12-yard run with 2:58 left. On third-and-8 at the Michigan 34 with 1:18 left, Michigan was called for holding, a 10-yard penalty and a first down. On the next play Rocco Becht hit Chase Sowell for a 24-yard touchdown. Final 21-18.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Wisconsin +2.5 (card line: UCLA −2.5). Wisconsin lost by 10. Missed by 7.5. The Cover Writer projected UCLA 20, Wisconsin 19.
Wisconsin got within 10-7 in the third. Anthony Woods' 3-yard run with 11:31 left made it 17-7, and Wisconsin's next drive ended on a fourth-down run near midfield.
Missed: Letdown Watch on Oregon −7 (card line). Oregon won by 3. Missed by 4.

Nebraska led 14-6 after Anthony Colandrea's 6-yard run with 7 seconds left in the third. Oregon won on a 4-yard touchdown pass from Dylan Raiola to Jamari Johnson and a two-point pass with 28 seconds left, but a 3-point win does not cover 7.
Missed: Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Florida Atlantic +2.5 (card line: Army −2.5). Florida Atlantic lost by 32. Missed by 29.5.
It was 14-14 late in the first quarter, and Army led 35-14 at the half. Cale Hellums ran for five touchdowns.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Next Man Up on Temple −19.5 (card line). Temple lost by 7. Missed by 26.5. The Cover Writer projected Temple 33, Charlotte 12.

The Cover Writer's case was Temple's healthier offense and wind gusts around 40 mph keeping the score down. Charlotte won by 7. Conner Harrell ran for two touchdowns and threw for two. Temple's next drive, down 35-28, ended on a fourth-down sack at the Charlotte 45.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 46.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 69. Missed by 22.5.
The total passed 46.5 on Harrell's 9-yard touchdown pass to Gus McGee with 14:12 left. The final total was 69.
Missed: Next Man Up and Follow The Money on Rice +4.5 (card line: Tulsa −4.5). Rice lost by 21. Missed by 16.5.
Rice led 17-7 on Jacurri Brown's runs of 50 and 78 yards. Tulsa scored the last 31 points, finishing with Trequan Jones' 45-yard run and a two-point run with 3:39 left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 46.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 46). The final total was 55. Missed by 8.5.
Sevion Morrison's 6-yard touchdown catch with 10:06 left made it 47 points even with the missed extra point. The final total was 55.
Missed: The Formula and In The Trenches on Kent State +20.5 (card line: South Florida −20.5). Kent State lost by 27. Missed by 6.5.
South Florida led only 17-2 after three quarters. Cameron Seldon's 36-yard touchdown catch early in the fourth made it 24-2 and put USF past 20.5. A safety with 11 seconds left made the final 29-2.
Missed: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on UTSA −6.5 (card line). UTSA won by 4. Missed by 2.5. The Cover Writer projected UTSA 32, Navy 24.

There were four lead changes in the fourth quarter. UTSA won on Owen McCown's 41-yard touchdown pass to A'Marion Peterson with 2:24 left. That was a 4-point lead, and UTSA needed 7. It got one more chance, and Peterson was stopped on fourth down at the Navy 10 with 10 seconds left.
Missed: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Bowling Green −6.5 (card line). Bowling Green lost by 1. Missed by 7.5. The Cover Writer projected Bowling Green 27, Ball State 20.

Bowling Green tied it 17-17 with 1:12 left, and 11 seconds later D'kyah Banks returned a fumble 35 yards for a touchdown and a 24-17 lead. At that moment Bowling Green −6.5 was covering by half a point. Ball State answered with Keldric Luster's 20-yard touchdown pass to Eli Hohlt on the last play of regulation. In overtime Bowling Green scored first, on Austyn Dendy's 4-yard run, and Ball State won 32-31 on TJ Horton's 1-yard run and Luster's two-point pass to Alex Scherle.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 42.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 40). The final total was 43. Missed by 0.5.

Every side pick in this game pushed at 7. The Under missed by half a point. It was 18-18 and 36 points after Oliver Hautanen's 29-yard field goal with 2 seconds left. In overtime, Jason Wright's 15-yard touchdown pass to Clint Walker and the extra point made it 25-18 and 43 total. The kick after the touchdown was the half point.
Missed: Next Man Up on Eastern Michigan +7 (card line: Toledo −7). Eastern Michigan lost by 20. Missed by 13.
Toledo led 31-7 at the half and 34-14 at the end. Eastern Michigan's two fourth-quarter drives into Toledo territory ended on fourth-down sacks.
Missed: Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Akron +9.5 (card line: Miami (OH) −9.5). Akron lost by 20. Missed by 10.5.
Miami's Blayne Myrick returned an interception 36 yards for a touchdown late in the third for 27-7. Akron threw two more interceptions early in the fourth.
Missed: The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Sacramento State +15.5 (card line: Ohio −15.5). Sacramento State lost by 41. Missed by 25.5.
Ohio led 27-0 at the half. Nick Poulos' 67-yard touchdown pass to Preston Bowman early in the third made it 34-0, and it was 41-0 after three quarters.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 46.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 55. Missed by 8.5.
Sacramento State's only touchdown, Brian Salazar Jr.'s 38-yard pass to Kenyon Shabazz with 12:24 left, made it 48 points. Ohio added one more touchdown. The final total was 55.
Missed: Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Georgia State +9.5 (card line: James Madison −9.5). Georgia State lost by 27. Missed by 17.5.
Camden Coleman threw first-half touchdown passes of 20 and 19 yards, and James Madison led 35-10 at the half.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Troy +3 (card line: Louisiana −3). Troy lost by 27. Missed by 24.
Louisiana led 19-0 at the half. Troy's only score was a 23-yard run, and the extra point failed.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Southern Miss +6.5 (card line: Arkansas State −6.5). Southern Miss lost by 10. Missed by 3.5. The Cover Writer projected Arkansas State 35, Southern Miss 30.

Arkansas State led 16-7 at the half and 23-7 early in the fourth. Steven Robinson's 1-yard run cut it to 23-13 with 10:02 left, and the two-point run failed. Southern Miss got the ball back and threw incomplete on fourth down.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 61.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 65). The final total was 36. Missed by 25.5.
The Cover Writer expected two struggling defenses to give up plenty of points. The game produced 36.
Missed: The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on UL Monroe +15.5 (card line: Louisiana Tech −15.5). UL Monroe lost by 24. Missed by 8.5.
It was scoreless at the half. Louisiana Tech's third touchdown, Brayden Bockler's 2-yard catch from Blake Baker with 9:18 left, made it 21-0. ULM's last drive ended on downs at the Tech 19.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 55.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 59). The final total was 24. Missed by 31.5.
The game produced 24 points. A blocked field goal at the end of the first half kept it 0-0.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Follow The Money on Northern Illinois +7.5 (card line: Wyoming −7.5). Northern Illinois lost by 18. Missed by 10.5. The Cover Writer projected Wyoming 24, Northern Illinois 18.
Tyler Hughes ran for four touchdowns.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 42.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 42). The final total was 64. Missed by 21.5.
The total passed 42.5 in the third quarter on Telly Johnson Jr.'s 13-yard run and two-point conversion. The final total was 64.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on UNLV +1.5 (card line: Air Force −1.5). UNLV lost by 10. Missed by 8.5. The Cover Writer projected UNLV 23, Air Force 22.

The Cover Writer's case was UNLV's defense against an Air Force option run by a newer quarterback. Evan Medders ran for three touchdowns, and his 32-yarder early in the fourth put Air Force ahead 27-24. UNLV fumbled on its next drive, and Air Force scored the next two touchdowns.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 47.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 72. Missed by 24.5.
Medders' 32-yard run also took the total to 51. The final total was 72.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on North Dakota State −14.5 (card line). North Dakota State won by 14. Missed by 0.5.

North Dakota State won by 14 and needed 15. The missing point was its own blocked extra point before halftime. The Bison also scored on a 100-yard return of a missed Nevada field goal on the last play of the half and on a defensive two-point return. Reis Kessel's 12-yard catch early in the fourth made it 31-17, and nobody scored after that.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 42.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 40). The final total was 48. Missed by 5.5.
Kessel's touchdown made the total 48. The missed-field-goal return and the defensive two-point play accounted for 9 of those points.
Missed: Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on UTEP +7 (card line: San José State −7). UTEP lost by 13. Missed by 6.
San José State led 24-3 early in the fourth. UTEP's touchdown and two-point pass made it 24-11, and its last real drive ended on a fourth-down incompletion into the end zone with 1:49 left.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on New Mexico −14.5 (card line). New Mexico won by 11. Missed by 3.5. The Cover Writer projected New Mexico 29, Hawai'i 12.

New Mexico trailed 10-0 at the half and won by 11. Scottre Humphrey's 49-yard touchdown run with 3:24 left made it 21-10. New Mexico got the ball back on T. Combs' interception with 2:53 left and did not score again.
Missed: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Oregon State −18.5 (card line). Oregon State won by 18. Missed by 0.5. The Cover Writer projected Oregon State 35, Washington State 16.

Oregon State led 41-22 with nine minutes left, covering by half a point. Owen Eshelman's 20-yard run and two-point pass with 1:37 left made it 41-30. Cornell Hatcher Jr.'s 16-yard run 21 seconds later made it 48-30, an 18-point margin.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 52.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 51). The final total was 78. Missed by 25.5.
The card noted that Washington State had benched its quarterback. The teams scored 78.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Fresno State −7.5 (card line). Fresno State lost by 3. Missed by 10.5. The Cover Writer projected Fresno State 27, San Diego State 18.

San Diego State won outright. Fresno State tied it 23-23 with 5:02 left on Julius Gillick's 2-yard run, and the extra point failed. Cooper DiLeva kicked a 53-yard field goal with 57 seconds left to win it.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 45.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 49. Missed by 3.5.
Gillick's touchdown made the total 46, and DiLeva's kick made it 49.
Same rules as Part 1: card line at kickoff, and a push counts as neither. Pushes are noted under their games and counted as neither.
Hit: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on LSU −17.5 (card line). LSU won by 31. Covered by 13.5.
Card cases: Next Man Up, the injury report tilted toward LSU; Follow The Money, betting-market signals pointed to LSU; In The Trenches, LSU rated stronger on both lines of scrimmage.
The input that held up was the quarterback change. Leavitt's 6-yard touchdown pass to Malik Elzy with 31 seconds left in the third made it 31-0.
Hit: the Cover Writer on Under 55.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 52). The final total was 31. Hit by 24.5.
The card's reasons: the total had dropped from 59.5 to 55.5, Taylor was out, and gusts around 27 mph were forecast. The game finished with 31 points, and the Under was never close.
Hit: In The Trenches on Florida +11.5 (card line: Texas −11.5). Florida won by 3. Covered by 14.5.
Card cases: In The Trenches, Florida rated stronger on both lines of scrimmage.
Florida won outright. Texas's last drive ended when M. Graham sacked Manning and forced a fumble with about two minutes left.

Hit: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on The Citadel +46.5 (card line: Texas A&M −46.5). The Citadel lost by 41. Covered by 5.5. The Cover Writer projected Texas A&M 50, The Citadel 6.
The Cover Writer's card said: "Texas A&M wins by 44, but The Citadel stays inside the 46.5-point spread and covers."

Card cases: Next Man Up, the injury report tilted toward The Citadel; Follow The Money, no big betting moves, with the money tilting slightly to The Citadel; In The Trenches, The Citadel looked stronger up front, though the FCS team's stats are hard to compare.
Texas A&M scored one touchdown in the fourth quarter, Gregory's catch, and stopped at 41.
Hit: the Cover Writer on Under 56.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 56). The final total was 41. Hit by 15.5.
A&M controlled it, as the card said, and the game ended with 41 points.
Hit: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Auburn +19.5 (card line: Georgia −19.5). Auburn won by 3. Covered by 22.5. The Cover Writer projected Georgia 33, Auburn 14.
The Cover Writer's card said: "Auburn's rest and Georgia's missing receivers help the Tigers a little."
Card cases: The Formula, season-long power ratings rated Auburn better than the spread; Next Man Up, the injury report tilted toward Auburn; Letdown Watch, rest and travel favored Auburn.
Auburn never trailed by more than 14 and led most of the day. Byrum Brown's 5-yard run in the third made it 24-14, and McPherson's kick won it outright.
Hit: Follow The Money on Ole Miss −5.5 (card line). Ole Miss won by 28. Covered by 22.5.
